newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan, India set talks for June 19-22.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan, India set talks for June 19-22.

text.p: India and Pakistan have decided that the next round of talks between their foreign ministry officials will be held in Islamabad on June 19-22, Pakistan Foreign Minister Gohar Ayub Khan said on Sunday.
The last session between officials was in New Delhi in March, marking a resumption of the dialogue between the two countries after a three-year hiatus.
Prime Ministers Nawaz Sharif of Pakistan and Inder Kumar Gujral of India agreed on the upcoming meeting when they attended a regional summit in the Maldives earlier this month.

Khan said officials would discuss what Pakistan regards as the "core issue" -- their dispute over the Himalayan region of Jammu and Kashmir, the cause of two of the three wars between the two countries since independence from Britain in 1947.
Pakistan, which controls one-third of Kashmir, wants the dispute settled through a U.N.-mandated plebiscite to allow the predominantly Moslem Kashmiris to decide which country to join.
India, which is fighting a separatist revolt in the two-thirds of Kashmir it rules, rejects the idea of a plebiscite as it claims the whole of the region.
Some of the militant groups fighting Indian rule want to Kashmir to become an independent state.
